purpose: A bounded method for deciding which home service-contract products an agent can lawfully and honestly carry, how each product's obligor, administrator, term, caps, service-fee and compensation mechanics actually work, which distribution channels (real-estate closing, direct-to-homeowner, property-manager portfolios, trade partnerships) fit that agent's authorization and capacity, and what compliance class, disclosure placement and economics attach to each channel before a single contract is written.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
the agent sells contracts issued by third-party obligors and never performs, adjudicates or funds a repair; claim outcomes are the obligor's decision under the written contract

home service contracts are regulated at the state or provincial level, the applicable class and the registration, filing and disclosure duties differ by jurisdiction and change over time, so every regulatory statement here names a class of obligation to verify locally rather than a current specific rule

all money quantities - contract price, service call fee, caps, commission, overrides, renewal amounts - are treated as mechanisms with named drivers and a per-deal verification path, never as stated figures
the reader is, or intends to become, an authorized representative of one or more obligors and has or will obtain access to their actual product schedules, rate schedules and compensation exhibits
this knowledge base is educational and operational for the seller; it is not personalized legal, insurance, tax or financial advice for any homeowner, landlord or agent
exclusions: line-by-line interpretation of covered systems, exclusion clauses, waiting periods and pre-existing-condition language, and the disclosure-first contract-reading conversation held with a specific homeowner - that is the coverage-terms knowledge base this one hands off to

matching a plan tier to a particular home's realistic risk profile from system age, prior repairs and inspection findings, and the per-client documentation packet built during that conversation - also coverage-terms territory

renewal economics, honest renewal and non-renewal conversations, claims-experience guidance for a client, denial handling, reputation management and retention of the in-force book - that is the renewals and claims knowledge base
adjudicating, appealing or predicting the outcome of any individual claim; the obligor decides claims under the contract and this knowledge base never asserts what will or will not be paid

asserting the current registration, licensing, filing, cancellation or disclosure rules of any named jurisdiction; obligations are named as classes to verify with the applicable regulator, the obligor's compliance desk and counsel

quoting specific contract prices, service call fees, cap amounts, commission rates, override percentages, renewal multiples or market sizes as facts; every such quantity appears only as a mechanism with its drivers and its verification path
personalized legal, insurance, tax or financial advice to a homeowner, landlord, property manager or agent
performing repairs, running the obligor's contractor network or field dispatch, and the obligor's own underwriting, pricing and reserving decisions

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SERVICE_CONTRACT_PRODUCT_FRAME states the category and its wear-failure trigger against insurance, manufacturer warranty and maintenance plans; OBLIGOR_ADMIN_STRUCTURE_MAP names obligor, administrator, backing and the seller's non-obligation; REPRESENTATION_BOUNDARY_RULE states the outer limit of what may be said

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: JURISDICTION_REGULATORY_CLASS names the obligation classes and the questions to put to the regulator, obligor and counsel without asserting a current specific rule; SELLER_AUTHORIZATION_STACK states what the seller's own authorization file must contain

competency_questions.question: How is an obligor's plan line-up structured into tiers and options, and what does moving up a tier actually change about the product?

competency_questions.question: When does coverage start and end for this order, and what happens to the money if someone cancels?

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CHANNEL_COMPLIANCE_MATRIX defines the channel-by-obligation-class matrix with a named owner, source and future review date per cell, plus the trigger list that forces re-review

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CHANNEL_CONTRIBUTION_MODEL compares channels on measured contribution per hour including chargeback and dispute load; ENROLLMENT_HANDOFF_PACKET lists the packet contents and the hard gate conditions that stop an order

glossary.definition: A term agreement under which a named obligor promises to repair or replace specified home systems and appliances that fail from normal wear, subject to stated limits and conditions, in exchange for a contract fee and a per-visit service fee; commonly marketed as a home warranty even though it is neither an insurance policy nor a manufacturer warranty.

The legal entity contractually bound to perform under the contract - to repair, replace or pay within the stated limits. The brand on the marketing is not always the obligor; the obligor is the entity the contract names, and it is the party whose failure to perform is a breach.

The entity that receives claim calls, authorizes work and dispatches contractors on the obligor's behalf. It may be the obligor itself or a separate company, and it is usually the party a client actually experiences, which makes its responsiveness a reputational input for the selling agent.

The arrangement standing behind the obligor's promise to perform - commonly a contractual liability insurance policy or a funded reserve, depending on what the jurisdiction requires and what the obligor has filed. It is the answer to what happens if the obligor cannot pay, and its class should be identified per product and verified locally.

The amount the contract holder pays each time a technician is dispatched, generally applied per trade rather than per visit; it behaves like a deductible, is often selectable at purchase in inverse relation to the contract fee, and suppresses small claims when set high.

A ceiling on what the obligor will pay across all claims in a term, sitting above the per-item and category sub-limits. Confusing an aggregate with a per-item limit is one of the most common and most damaging quoting errors in this business.

The set of independent trade contractors the administrator dispatches to authorized jobs in a given area. Network depth in the specific counties a seller works determines real-world dispatch speed and is a diligence input rather than a marketing claim.

A feature some products offer in the transaction channel where limited coverage runs for the seller of the home during the listing period once the contract is ordered, used as an inducement to order early rather than at the settlement table.

The initial period after purchase during which the contract holder may cancel on more favourable refund terms, after which refunds are typically pro-rata less an administrative amount and less claims paid. The length, the refund basis and whether it is mandated differ by jurisdiction and product, so both are read off the actual contract and verified locally.

The reversal of compensation already paid to the seller when a contract is cancelled within a stated window, fails to fund, or meets another condition in the compensation exhibit; it is a structural part of the compensation mechanism rather than an exception to it.

nodes.definition: Fix what is actually being sold before anything else is decided. A home service contract is a term agreement under which a named obligor promises to repair or replace specified home systems and appliances that fail from normal wear, subject to stated limits and conditions, in exchange for a contract fee plus a per-visit service fee. It is not homeowners insurance, which responds to sudden accidental loss to the structure and its contents; it is not a manufacturer warranty, which covers defects in one specific new product for a period set by the maker; and it is not a maintenance subscription, which buys scheduled service rather than a remedy for failure. The frame is load-bearing because it decides what the product may be called in marketing, which regulator is likely to class it, who is liable to perform, and the outer edge of what a seller may honestly promise. Getting the category wrong produces insurance-flavoured marketing, buyers who believe they bought blanket protection, and the vertical's signature failure: selling peace of mind that everything is covered.

included: the definitional boundary between service contract, insurance policy, manufacturer warranty and maintenance plan
the failure-from-normal-wear trigger as the product's core promise
the naming and marketing vocabulary discipline that follows from the category
excluded: interpreting a specific contract's covered-item list and exclusion clauses, which belongs to the coverage-terms knowledge base
predicting whether any particular failure will be paid

pros.claim: A crisp category definition gives the seller a defensible answer to the buyer's first real question and prevents the is-this-insurance misstatement
pros.example: answering a buyer who asks whether the plan replaces their homeowners policy by naming the wear-failure versus sudden-loss difference and pointing at both documents

cons.claim: The clean category line is blurrier in practice than in training material, because obligors bundle riders that look insurance-like and some jurisdictions class the whole product under the insurance code anyway
cons.example: a plan with an optional roof-leak rider sold by an agent trained to say this is never insurance

failure_modes: marketing the product with insurance vocabulary that invites both regulatory attention and expectation problems
letting covers your home stand as the working definition so the buyer hears blanket protection
assuming the category answer from one state applies everywhere the seller works
acceptance_tests: the seller can state in one sentence what triggers the obligor's duty to perform and name two adjacent products this is not, without using insurance as a synonym
revisit_triggers: an obligor adds a rider that changes the category story
a jurisdiction reclassifies the product or issues guidance on how it may be described

base.update_signal: an obligor product filing or a regulator bulletin restates what class this product belongs to or how it may be described

nodes.definition: Draw the party map for every product carried: who is the obligor bound to perform, who is the administrator that takes the claim call and authorizes and dispatches work, what backs the obligor's performance as named in the contract or its filings, who owns the contractor network, and where the selling agent sits, which is almost always as an authorized representative with no duty to perform anything. This is the most load-bearing artifact in the subdomain because it answers the buyer's fair question - if you sell me this and the furnace dies, who actually has to fix it - and because it tells the seller precisely which promises are not theirs to make. It also identifies whose failure will land on the seller anyway: an obligor that cannot fund replacements, or an administrator with a thin network in the property's county, becomes the seller's reputation problem while remaining someone else's legal duty.

included: identifying obligor, administrator, backing arrangement, network owner and seller role per carried product
locating each of those parties in the contract text and on the order form
stating the seller's non-obligation to perform as a fact given to buyers
excluded: evaluating an obligor's financial strength and field record in depth, which is the diligence screen
advocating an individual claim once it has been filed, which belongs to the renewals and claims knowledge base

pros.claim: Knowing the party map lets the seller answer the who-fixes-it question accurately and refuse promises that belong to another party
pros.example: telling a buyer that the administrator authorizes the repair under the contract and the seller's role ends at placing the order correctly

cons.claim: The map is only as good as the paperwork, and obligor, administrator and network relationships change without notice reaching a small selling agent
cons.example: an administrator change discovered from a client complaint about a new claim phone number rather than from the obligor

failure_modes: the seller describing themselves as the party who will fix things
assuming the brand on the marketing is the obligor when the contract names a different legal entity
never checking what stands behind the obligor's promise
acceptance_tests: for each carried product the seller can point to the contract clause naming the obligor and the administrator, name what backs performance, and state the seller's own role in one sentence
revisit_triggers: an obligor changes administrator, network or backing arrangement
a contract revision changes the named obligating entity

base.update_signal: the named obligor, administrator or backing arrangement changes on a new contract version or an obligor notice

nodes.definition: Before selling into the jurisdiction where a property sits, determine which regulatory class the product falls into there and which obligation attaches to which party. The classes to identify are whether the jurisdiction handles home service contracts under a dedicated service-contract statute or under its insurance code; whether the obligor must register, file its forms or maintain a specified backing such as contractual liability insurance or a funded reserve; whether the administrator must be registered; whether the person selling needs a licence, an appointment or merely a recorded authorization; and what mandatory contract disclosures, cancellation rights and record-retention duties apply. This knowledge base names those classes and the questions to put to the regulator, the obligor's compliance desk and counsel; it never asserts what a specific jurisdiction currently requires, because these rules differ by state and are amended. The screen runs per property jurisdiction rather than per agent location, because the property's jurisdiction usually governs, and it is re-run whenever the map of where you sell changes.

included: identifying the classes of statute, registration, licensing, disclosure, cancellation and retention obligation that may apply
the question set put to the regulator, the obligor and counsel, and the dated record of their answers
running the screen per property jurisdiction and again on expansion
excluded: stating the current specific rules, fees or filings of any named jurisdiction - verify current rules in your jurisdiction with the regulator and counsel
the seller's own contractual authorization from the obligor, which is the authorization stack

pros.claim: Running the class screen before any pipeline is built prevents committing to a market where the product or the seller is not authorized
pros.example: discovering during the screen that an obligor has no filing for a neighbouring state before a listing-agent partnership there is signed

cons.claim: Class-level answers require verification work per jurisdiction and per obligor, which slows market entry and can stall a deal already in motion
cons.example: an out-of-state referral arriving while the screen for that state is still open

failure_modes: assuming an obligor's authority covers every state the seller can reach
treating a marketing brochure's compliance claim as the compliance answer
asserting a specific rule from memory or from a peer instead of verifying it with the regulator and counsel
acceptance_tests: for every jurisdiction in the pipeline there is a dated record naming the obligation classes identified, the source consulted, the person who consulted it, and the questions still open
revisit_triggers: a new jurisdiction enters the pipeline
a regulator bulletin or statutory amendment is announced for a jurisdiction already in the book
an obligor changes its filing or registration status

base.update_signal: a jurisdiction amends its service-contract statute, registration or disclosure requirements, or an obligor's filing status in that jurisdiction changes

nodes.definition: Assemble and keep current the stack of authorizations that lets this seller offer this product in this jurisdiction through this channel. The stack contains the written representative or producer agreement with the obligor, which defines territory, sellable products, compensation, approved materials and termination; whatever licence or registration class the jurisdiction attaches to selling the product; the marketing-material approval rights the agreement reserves; the disclosure-delivery duties the agreement pushes down onto the seller; and the interaction with any other licence the seller holds - most sharply a real-estate licence, which brings its own conduct, interest-disclosure and referral rules into the closing channel. The stack is a file with dates, not a memory: appointment letters, effective and expiry dates, approved material versions in use, and the named contact at the obligor's compliance desk. Everything downstream hangs off it, because a channel the authorization does not cover cannot be built, material outside the approved set cannot be sent, and compensation on business written under a lapsed appointment is frequently not payable at all.

included: representative or producer agreement terms that bind the seller, including territory, products, approved materials and termination
the licence or registration class the seller must personally hold or have verified
interaction with a real-estate or other professional licence already held
the dated authorization file itself and its renewal calendar
excluded: the obligor's own registration and filing duties, which sit in the jurisdiction screen
asserting which specific licence a named jurisdiction requires - verify current rules in your jurisdiction

pros.claim: A current authorization file turns can-I-sell-this-here into a lookup rather than an argument in the middle of a deal
pros.example: checking the territory clause of the representative agreement before accepting a referral two counties outside the usual area

cons.claim: Maintaining the stack is administrative overhead that multiplies with every added obligor, jurisdiction and channel
cons.example: three carried obligors with three different approved-material rules producing three parallel marketing approval queues

failure_modes: writing business under a lapsed appointment and losing the compensation on it
using unapproved marketing material because the approval queue was slow
ignoring the conduct and disclosure rules of a real-estate licence while working closings
acceptance_tests: the authorization file shows, per obligor and per jurisdiction, a current agreement, the approved material versions actually in use, and the next renewal or review date
revisit_triggers: an appointment renews, lapses or is terminated
the seller adds an obligor, a jurisdiction or a channel
the seller obtains or gives up another professional licence

base.update_signal: an appointment, territory grant, approved-material list or personal licence status changes

nodes.definition: Set the outer boundary of what this seller will say, in advance and in writing, so it does not have to be decided under objection pressure. The rule has three parts. First, the document governs: nothing is represented that the contract does not say, and where a buyer's question is answered by a clause, the clause is shown rather than paraphrased into a promise. Second, claim outcomes belong to the obligor: the seller may explain how the claim process works and what the contract states, and may never predict, guarantee or imply an approval, a replacement rather than a repair, or a particular contractor. Third, the category's characteristic overstatements are named and banned across every channel and every script - everything is covered, guaranteed replacement, it pays for itself, your warranty is expiring - along with any framing that manufactures fear about a specific system failing. This is a first-class product of the subdomain rather than an aside, because the vertical's core ethical failure is not misquoting a price; it is letting a buyer leave the table believing the contract promises more than it does.

included: the document-governs rule and the habit of showing the clause
the ban list of category overstatements and fear-selling framings applied to every script and template
the statement that claims are adjudicated by the obligor under the contract, not by the seller
excluded: the clause-by-clause disclosure conversation and its per-client documentation, which belong to the coverage-terms knowledge base
advocating a filed claim or handling a denial, which belongs to the renewals and claims knowledge base

pros.claim: A pre-committed language boundary survives the pressure of a live objection far better than judgement improvised in the moment
pros.example: answering so if the air conditioner dies you will replace it by opening the cap and covered-cause language instead of saying yes

cons.claim: Refusing the reassuring answer costs sales to competitors who give it, and some buyers read precision as evasiveness
cons.example: losing a closing-table order to a rival who answers that everything is covered without qualification

failure_modes: softening a stated limit into a promise when the objection gets hard
predicting a claim outcome in order to close
importing expiring-warranty urgency framing from a marketing vendor's template
acceptance_tests: every script, mailer and email template in use has been checked against the ban list with a date, and each carried product has a clause pointer prepared for the three questions buyers ask most
revisit_triggers: a new template or vendor script enters use
a client complaint alleges an overstatement
a contract revision changes what a cited clause says

base.update_signal: a complaint, a contract revision or a new script reveals a representation the boundary does not yet cover

nodes.definition: Learn how each carried obligor builds its line-up, as structure rather than as brochure adjectives. The recurring shape is a split between a systems plan covering the mechanicals the house runs on, an appliance plan covering the equipment inside it, and a combined plan; a tier ladder above that, where a higher tier typically buys higher item limits, more included items or fewer conditions rather than a different promise; and a separately priced option layer for things like pool and spa equipment, well and septic components, additional refrigeration, roof-leak riders and modification or upgrade allowances, each of which usually carries conditions of its own. The working artifact is a dated per-obligor mechanics sheet stating, for every tier and option currently sellable, what is added, which limit moves and what condition attaches. This node is about the shape of the product line; deciding which tier a particular home should buy is the coverage-terms knowledge base's judgement, not this one's.

included: the systems, appliance and combined structure of a line-up
how the tier ladder changes limits, included items and conditions
the separately priced option layer and its conditions
the dated per-obligor mechanics sheet as the artifact
excluded: recommending a tier for a specific home's risk profile, which is the coverage-terms knowledge base
interpreting exclusion language item by item

pros.claim: A mechanics sheet lets the seller answer tier questions from structure instead of from adjectives, which makes an upgrade conversation defensible
pros.example: showing that moving up a tier raises a stated item limit and adds a modification allowance rather than saying it simply covers more

cons.claim: Line-ups are revised on the obligor's schedule, so the sheet decays quietly and a stale sheet is more dangerous than none
cons.example: quoting a separately priced option that the obligor folded into the base tier in its last revision

failure_modes: selling the tier the seller understands best rather than the one the line-up actually supports
treating an option as included because a competitor includes it
letting the sheet go undated so nobody knows whether it is current
acceptance_tests: each carried obligor has a dated mechanics sheet covering every tier and option currently sellable, and the date is inside the obligor's revision cycle
revisit_triggers: the obligor publishes a revised line-up, rate schedule or option list

base.update_signal: an obligor publishes a revised plan line-up, adds an option, or moves an option into a base tier

nodes.definition: Treat caps as arithmetic rather than adjectives. These contracts limit the obligor's exposure through stacked devices: a per-item or per-system limit, narrower sub-limits on particular categories such as ductwork, refrigerant handling or plumbing behind walls, a per-term aggregate across all claims, and separate allowances or exclusions for code upgrades, permits, disposal, crane or attic access and the modifications needed to fit a replacement into an older installation. The seller's competence is to be able to walk any cap table and produce the worst-case arithmetic for a buyer: what the contract pays at most for this item, what the buyer would owe beyond it, and which surrounding costs sit outside the limit entirely. Because replacement costs move with equipment and labour markets while cap tables move on the obligor's revision cycle, the honest framing is always the mechanism - here is the stated limit, here is what a replacement of this class of equipment runs with local contractors, here is the gap - and never an invented figure recited from memory.

included: per-item, sub-category and aggregate limit mechanics and how they stack
the surrounding allowances for code, permits, disposal, access and modification and whether each sits inside or outside the limit
the worst-case exposure arithmetic shown to a buyer before signature
excluded: stating any specific cap amount or replacement price as a fact - always read the buyer's actual cap table and verify local costs
deciding whether a given failure is a covered cause, which is coverage-terms territory

pros.claim: Cap arithmetic converts the most common post-claim grievance in this business into a pre-sale conversation the buyer can still act on
pros.example: showing that an item limit plus separate disposal and modification allowances still leaves a gap on a high-efficiency system replacement in that county

cons.claim: The arithmetic can talk a buyer out of a plan that would still have served them, and it takes time the closing channel rarely offers
cons.example: a buyer declining after seeing the gap on one large system while ignoring the several smaller failures the plan would have handled

failure_modes: quoting a cap from memory or from a competitor's comparison sheet
presenting an aggregate cap as if it were a per-item limit
omitting the allowances that sit outside the limit so the gap looks smaller than it is
acceptance_tests: for each carried tier the seller can produce worst-case gap arithmetic on a major system using only that contract's own cap table and a locally verified replacement cost range
revisit_triggers: the obligor revises its cap table or allowance structure
local replacement or labour costs shift enough to change the gap story

base.update_signal: a revised cap table, a changed allowance structure, or client claim experience showing the gap arithmetic was understated

nodes.definition: The per-visit trade service call fee is the product's second price and behaves like a deductible. The contract holder pays it each time a technician is dispatched, it is commonly applied per trade rather than per visit so a single problem needing two trades costs twice, and it is frequently selectable at purchase with an inverse relationship to the contract fee - a lower per-visit fee makes the contract cost more, a higher one makes it cost less. The seller must be able to explain the crossover mechanism, meaning how many dispatches in a term make the lower-fee option cheaper in total, and must be able to name the behavioural consequence honestly: a high fee suppresses small claims, which is precisely why a plan bought for its low headline price can end up feeling useless to the buyer. This is also where the seller's own interest enters the room, because the fee option changes the contract price and therefore, under most compensation schedules, the base on which the seller is paid.

included: the fee-versus-contract-price inverse relationship and its crossover arithmetic
per-trade rather than per-visit application
the claim-suppression effect of a high fee stated plainly to the buyer
the fee option's effect on the compensation base as a disclosed mechanism
excluded: quoting any specific fee amount as a fact
deciding which fee level a particular household should choose, which belongs with the plan-fit conversation in the coverage-terms knowledge base

pros.claim: Explaining the crossover lets the buyer choose the fee level on their own expected usage instead of on the headline price alone
pros.example: walking through how many dispatches within one term would make the lower-fee option the cheaper of the two

cons.claim: The crossover is a projection built on failures nobody can forecast, so it can read as a sales device rather than as an aid
cons.example: a buyer who takes the low-fee option on that reasoning and then files no claims at all during the term

failure_modes: steering the buyer toward the fee option that maximises the compensation base
presenting the fee as per-visit when the contract applies it per trade
leaving the fee out of the total first-year cost picture entirely
acceptance_tests: every quote states the contract fee and the selected service fee separately as a first-year total, with the per-trade application noted in writing
revisit_triggers: the obligor changes its selectable fee levels or how the fee is applied

base.update_signal: the obligor changes its selectable service-fee levels, the price relationship, or the per-trade application rule

nodes.definition: Master when coverage starts, when it ends, and what happens to the money when someone stops it. The operationally decisive mechanics are the term length and whether the product is written annually, multi-year or month to month; the effective-date rule, which in the transaction channel commonly attaches to the recorded close rather than to the order date and in the direct channel commonly runs from purchase plus an initial period; whether an order placed during a listing carries any coverage for the home seller before the close; the cancellation architecture, typically an initial right-to-cancel window on more favourable terms followed by pro-rata refunds less an administrative amount and less claims paid; and who may cancel, which includes the contract holder, the obligor for non-payment, and the automatic unwind when a transaction fails to close. Effective-date error is the most expensive routine mistake in this subdomain because it is invisible until a claim lands in the gap, so the rule for each carried product is written down, applied from the document and re-confirmed whenever a closing date moves - never recalled.

included: term lengths and renewal-term structure as product mechanics
the effective-date rule per obligor and per channel and the gap risk between order, close and coverage start
cancellation windows, the refund computation mechanism and who may cancel
excluded: waiting-period and pre-existing-condition interpretation for a specific failure, which is the coverage-terms knowledge base
renewal pricing, renewal decisions and non-renewal conversations, which are the renewals knowledge base

pros.claim: A written effective-date rule per product prevents the coverage gap that turns an ordinary sale into a complaint nobody can fix afterwards
pros.example: re-confirming before a rescheduled closing whether coverage attaches on the original or the new recorded date

cons.claim: Effective-date and refund mechanics vary by obligor and by jurisdiction, so the seller carries a matrix rather than a rule and must re-check it on every product revision
cons.example: two carried obligors computing pro-rata refunds on different bases for the same cancellation month

failure_modes: telling a buyer coverage starts at the order when the contract attaches it to the recorded close
promising a full refund after the initial right-to-cancel window has passed
leaving a contract in force after a transaction failed to close
acceptance_tests: every order packet records the effective-date rule applied and the date it produces, and any deal whose closing date moves shows a re-confirmation entry
revisit_triggers: a closing date moves or a transaction fails
an obligor revises term, effective-date or refund mechanics
a jurisdiction changes required cancellation rights

base.update_signal: an obligor revises term, effective-date or cancellation mechanics, or a jurisdiction changes the cancellation rights it requires

nodes.definition: Decide which obligors are worth carrying at all, and write down in advance the evidence on which you would stop. The screen covers how the obligor's performance is funded and backed; its registration and filing standing in the jurisdictions you actually sell; the depth of the contractor network in the specific counties where your properties sit, because a thin network becomes slow dispatch and angry clients regardless of what the contract says; the administrator's claim intake and authorisation responsiveness; the complaint and denial pattern visible in regulator records, dispute filings and review platforms, read for pattern rather than for outrage; the escalation path a selling agent is actually given; and the stability of the contract terms themselves over recent revisions. The output is a carried-products shortlist with a written reason per product and explicit stop conditions. The asymmetry that makes this node matter is simple: the seller's reputation is built out of the obligor's field performance while the seller holds none of the obligor's authority.

included: backing and funding structure, registration standing, network depth by county, administrator responsiveness, complaint pattern and agent escalation path
the carried-products shortlist with written reasons and stop conditions
periodic re-screening of products already carried
excluded: asserting any named obligor's financial condition or complaint record as a fact - read current primary sources for yourself
handling an individual client's claim escalation, which is the renewals and claims knowledge base

pros.claim: Screening before carrying prevents building a book on a product whose field performance the seller cannot survive commercially
pros.example: declining a high-paying product after finding its network in the target county consists of a handful of contractors

cons.claim: Thorough diligence narrows the line-up and often removes the best-compensating product from the menu entirely
cons.example: dropping the product with the strongest compensation exhibit after finding a persistent authorisation-delay pattern in dispute records

failure_modes: choosing a product on compensation and marketing support alone
reading a handful of angry reviews as the whole record, or dismissing a genuine pattern as noise
never re-screening a product once it is onboarded
acceptance_tests: every carried product has a dated diligence note covering backing, network depth in the counties actually sold, complaint pattern and the stop conditions that would end the relationship
revisit_triggers: a written stop condition is approached
the obligor changes ownership, administrator or network
client-reported field performance degrades over consecutive months

base.update_signal: regulator action, an ownership or administrator change, or a cluster of client-reported dispatch and authorisation failures on a carried product

nodes.definition: Be able to reconstruct any quote from its parts instead of reading a number off a portal and defending it. The price of a home service contract is assembled from the base tier; the property class, which may turn on single-family versus condominium versus multi-unit and on square-footage or age bands where the obligor uses them; the selected service-fee level; the chosen options; the channel, because transaction-channel pricing is frequently structured differently from direct-to-consumer; the term length and any multi-year or multi-property structure; and whatever regional cost factor the obligor applies. The discipline is to quote only from the current schedule for the actual property, to say out loud which components are driving the number, and to re-price rather than to adjust when any input changes. No price, discount or promotional structure is ever asserted from memory, from last season's schedule, or from a competitor's advertisement.

included: the component build of a quote and which inputs move it
channel-specific and property-class pricing structures as mechanisms
the re-price-on-input-change discipline and the recorded schedule version
excluded: stating any specific price, discount or promotional amount as a fact
the seller's own compensation, which is a separate mechanism with its own exhibit

pros.claim: Quoting from components lets the seller explain a price difference rather than defend it, which keeps a comparison conversation factual
pros.example: showing that a higher quote on a duplex is driven by the property class and unit count rather than by a markup

cons.claim: Component quoting exposes the buyer to complexity and invites line-item negotiation the seller usually has no authority to grant
cons.example: a buyer asking to strip out an option that the tier they want has bundled in

failure_modes: quoting from a superseded schedule or from another property's inputs
presenting a promotional price without its expiry and conditions
leaving the service-fee choice out of the total cost picture so the quote looks lower than the buyer's real first-year outlay
acceptance_tests: every quote records the schedule version, the property class, the fee level and the options used to build it, so it can be rebuilt later from the record
revisit_triggers: the obligor issues a new rate schedule, a channel-specific pricing change or a revised property-class definition

base.update_signal: a new rate schedule, a channel-specific pricing change, or a revised property-class definition from a carried obligor

nodes.definition: Know exactly how your money comes to exist, as a mechanism, and verify it deal by deal instead of assuming it. Compensation on a home service contract is created by the compensation exhibit of the representative agreement and typically combines some of: a flat amount per contract written, a share of the contract fee, a schedule that steps with volume or persistency, a differential on options or higher tiers, an override on business written by recruited sub-agents where the agreement and the jurisdiction permit it, and a renewal-year amount that is normally smaller than first year and conditioned on the contract staying in force and the agreement staying active. The chargeback mechanism is part of that structure rather than an exception to it: contracts cancelled inside a stated window, orders that never fund, and under some schedules claims-heavy business, reverse compensation already paid. The professional practice is to record an expected basis at order time and reconcile it against the actual statement, so that a schedule change or a mis-keyed channel code surfaces in weeks rather than at year end. No rate, amount, override or multiple is ever quoted as a fact - only the mechanism, its drivers, and where the seller reads their own numbers.

included: the components that can appear in a compensation exhibit and what triggers each
chargeback, funding and persistency conditions as part of the structure
the record-expectation-then-reconcile verification habit per deal
excluded: stating any commission rate, amount, override percentage or renewal multiple as a fact
renewal-book economics, valuation and retention strategy, which belong to the renewals knowledge base

pros.claim: Reconciling every statement against a recorded expectation catches schedule and coding errors while they can still be corrected
pros.example: spotting that a month of transaction-channel orders was paid on the direct-channel code

cons.claim: Seeing the differential clearly also means feeling its pull, and resisting it is a permanent tax on the seller's attention rather than a one-time decision
cons.example: noticing that the option with the better differential has quietly become the one the seller leads with

failure_modes: treating a recruiter's earnings illustration as the schedule
ignoring the chargeback window when a buyer is signalling second thoughts
letting the differential rather than the fit choose the recommendation
acceptance_tests: each written contract carries a recorded expected-compensation basis and is reconciled against the obligor's statement within one payment cycle, with variances logged
revisit_triggers: the compensation exhibit is amended
a statement disagrees with the recorded expectation
a new channel with its own source code is opened

base.update_signal: an amended compensation exhibit, a reconciliation variance, or a chargeback pattern concentrated in one channel

nodes.definition: Map the routes by which a home service contract reaches a buyer, and for each route name the buying moment, the decision maker, the person who actually influences the decision, the cycle length, the compliance class it drags in behind it and the servicing load it creates afterwards. The routes that matter here are the real-estate transaction, where the order is placed during a listing or escrow, decided under a closing deadline and influenced by an agent who is not the buyer; direct-to-homeowner, where there is no transaction event so the buying moment must be caught at a trigger such as a recent failure, an ageing system or a move-in anniversary; property managers and landlords, who buy a portfolio on repair-budget predictability and after-hours dispatch rather than on peace of mind; and trade partners such as heating, plumbing, electrical and appliance contractors and home inspectors, who meet the homeowner at the exact moment a failure is on their mind. Channels are not interchangeable pipes into the same market: each carries its own compliance class, its own disclosure difficulty and its own economics, which is why they are mapped and screened against the authorization file before any one of them is built.

included: the principal routes with their buying moments, decision makers, influencers and cycle lengths
the compliance class and post-sale servicing load each route drags in
screening each route for buildability against the current authorization file
excluded: the operating detail of each channel, which each channel node carries
the contribution model that ranks and sequences channels, which is the channel economics node

pros.claim: Mapping the buying moment stops a seller from applying a transaction-channel motion to a homeowner who has no transaction and no deadline
pros.example: dropping closing-deadline urgency language when the same offer is taken to a homeowner who is not moving

cons.claim: A map invites the seller to open more channels than they can service, and a half-built channel leaks reputation faster than no channel at all
cons.example: signing a property-manager portfolio while the transaction-channel order flow is still being handled by hand

failure_modes: treating every channel as a variation of the closing sale
opening a channel the current authorization does not actually cover
ignoring the servicing load a channel creates until it arrives
acceptance_tests: each mapped channel names its buying moment, decision maker, compliance class and servicing load, and is marked buildable or not buildable against the dated authorization file
revisit_triggers: the authorization file changes
a channel's buying moment shifts, for example a change in local transaction volume or the loss of a partner category

base.update_signal: a change in the seller's authorization, or a structural shift in a channel's buying moment such as local transaction volume or partner availability

nodes.definition: Operate the transaction channel on the escrow calendar rather than on the sales calendar. The mechanics are specific and unforgiving. The order is usually opened during the listing or once the property is in escrow; the payer may be the home seller as a concession, the buyer directly, or either of them through settlement; the invoice is commonly presented to the closing agent for payment from funds at close, which means the order has to be in the file before the settlement statement is finalised; some products offer limited coverage to the home seller during the listing period as an inducement to order early; the effective date generally attaches to the recorded close; and the introducing real-estate agent is recorded as the source, which is where compensation and compliance questions arrive immediately. The channel's advantages are volume, a natural buying moment and payment out of closing funds. Its structural hazard is exactly as blunt: the most deadline-compressed moment in a homeowner's year is where this product's caps, fees and exclusions most need to be surfaced.

included: order timing against listing, escrow and settlement cut-offs
payer structures and payment from closing funds
listing-period coverage as an ordering mechanism
source and agent-of-record recording and its downstream compensation and compliance effects
excluded: paying or receiving value from transaction partners, which is its own compliance node
the contract-reading conversation with the buyer, which belongs to the coverage-terms knowledge base

pros.claim: Payment from closing funds removes the buyer's cash objection and turns the purchase into a line item rather than a discretionary spend
pros.example: an order added to the settlement statement while the buyer's available cash is committed to the down payment and moving costs

cons.claim: Deadline compression is the strongest structural pressure against disclosure in this business, and the influencer in the room is compensated on the transaction closing rather than on the buyer's satisfaction a year later
cons.example: a buyer signing the order at the settlement table having never seen the cap table

failure_modes: missing the settlement-statement cut-off and losing the order
treating the transaction agent rather than the homeowner as the client whose interest governs
applying an effective-date rule from memory after a closing date has moved
acceptance_tests: every transaction-channel order records the payer, that the settlement cut-off was met, the effective-date rule applied, and the disclosure artifact delivered and acknowledged before signature
revisit_triggers: a closing date or payer changes
the obligor changes transaction-channel ordering or listing-coverage mechanics
a pattern of orders arriving after the settlement cut-off appears

base.update_signal: a change in the obligor's transaction-channel ordering mechanics, or a pattern of orders missing the settlement cut-off or the pre-signature acknowledgement

nodes.definition: Treat the value exchange with transaction partners as a compliance problem before treating it as a relationship problem. Several distinct bodies of rule can bear on paying, receiving or sharing anything of value in connection with a residential settlement: settlement-services anti-kickback and unearned-fee rules, state real-estate licensing conduct rules on referral compensation and disclosure of a licensee's interest, insurance-code anti-rebate and inducement rules where the jurisdiction classes the product that way, and the obligor's own agreement terms which often restrict what a representative may offer. Which of these apply, and how, depends on the jurisdiction, the parties and how the arrangement is papered, so the seller's job here is to identify the classes in play, obtain a review from counsel and the obligor's compliance desk before the arrangement starts, and keep a written record of what was agreed and what was actually paid. Structures that survive scrutiny - genuine marketing services at documented fair value, co-marketing with proportional cost sharing, or simply paying nothing - are preferred not because they are universally required but because informal per-deal cash never survives being asked about.

included: identifying which classes of rule may bear on a proposed arrangement
papering the arrangement and keeping a reconcilable payment record
preferring reviewable structures over informal per-deal value transfer
excluded: stating what any named jurisdiction currently permits or prohibits - obtain a current review from counsel and the obligor's compliance desk
the sales and ordering mechanics of the closing channel itself

pros.claim: Reviewing the structure before the relationship starts avoids an arrangement that must later be unwound with the partner and a regulator both watching
pros.example: converting a proposed per-order thank-you payment into a documented co-marketing arrangement before the first order is placed

cons.claim: The reviewable structure is slower and less attractive to partners than what looser competitors offer, and it can cost the relationship outright
cons.example: a high-volume listing agent moving to a rival who simply pays per order and asks no questions

failure_modes: agreeing to per-deal payment because a competitor does it
treating gifts, event sponsorship or lead purchases as outside the question
keeping no record of what was paid to whom and against what invoice
acceptance_tests: every transaction-partner arrangement has a written description, a documented review by counsel or the obligor's compliance desk, and a payment record that reconciles to it
revisit_triggers: a partner proposes a new arrangement or changes an existing one
a regulator or the obligor issues guidance touching referral compensation
a payment appears that does not reconcile to a reviewed structure

base.update_signal: new regulator or obligor guidance on referral compensation, or a partner proposal that does not fit an already-reviewed structure

nodes.definition: Sell to homeowners who are not in a transaction, which means there is no deadline, no third-party influencer and no closing funds - only a homeowner deciding whether to convert unpredictable repair costs into a predictable fee plus a per-dispatch charge. The channel runs on triggers rather than events: a recent failure, an ageing system, a move-in anniversary, the genuine expiry of a manufacturer warranty the homeowner actually holds, or a referral from a satisfied client. Its operating pieces are lead sourcing and consent, the contact-method compliance classes that bind outreach such as telephone solicitation and do-not-call rules, messaging and email consent rules, and home-solicitation rules with their own cancellation rights; material approval under the representative agreement; and a longer, lower-pressure conversation than a closing table can hold. This is also where the category's worst practices live - the mailer dressed as an expiring-warranty notice, the call that manufactures fear about one specific system - so the channel is built with the representation boundary wired into every script and template from the first day rather than bolted on after a complaint.

included: trigger-based prospecting and referral flow where no transaction event exists
contact-method compliance classes to identify and verify locally
script and template construction inside the representation boundary
the longer decision cycle and the follow-up discipline it needs
excluded: lead purchase provenance and consent recordkeeping, which is its own node
asserting the current telemarketing, messaging or home-solicitation rules of any jurisdiction

pros.claim: Without a deadline the buyer can actually read the contract before deciding, which produces better-set expectations and materially fewer later grievances
pros.example: sending the sample contract and cap table before a scheduled call rather than presenting them at signature

cons.claim: Acquisition is slower and costlier per contract, and the channel's reputation arrives already damaged by the deceptive mailers other sellers put in the same mailboxes
cons.example: a homeowner opening the call by asking whether this is the same outfit that sent the expiring-warranty notice

failure_modes: borrowing urgency devices from a vendor's template without checking them against the boundary
dialling a purchased list with no consent record behind it
manufacturing fear about one system in order to create a buying moment
acceptance_tests: every outbound template and script in the channel carries a dated check against the representation boundary and against the contact-method classes identified for the target jurisdiction
revisit_triggers: a new lead source, template or contact method is introduced
a complaint about outreach arrives
an applicable contact-method rule changes

base.update_signal: a change in applicable contact-method rules, a new outreach template, or a complaint pattern traced to this channel

nodes.definition: Sell to the party who manages repair cost and tenant complaints across a portfolio rather than to the person living in the house, because the buying logic is genuinely different. A property manager or landlord is buying budget predictability, after-hours dispatch capacity they do not want to staff, and a defensible answer to a tenant's repair demand - not peace of mind. The operating questions are who holds the contract, the owner or the manager acting as agent; who may place a claim and who pays the service fee when the tenant is the one who noticed the problem; how tenant-caused damage and failed access are treated given that these contracts respond to normal wear and require entry; how multi-property and per-door structures are written and billed; and how the manager's existing maintenance workflow and preferred vendors will coexist with the obligor's network. The channel is attractive for volume and concentration of renewals, and dangerous for the same reason, because one manager's bad experience moves an entire portfolio at once and a mismatch between the wear trigger and a tenant-damage reality generates disputes at scale.

included: portfolio and per-door contract structures and their billing
contract holder, claim placement and service-fee responsibility across owner, manager and tenant
structural fit and misfit against tenant-caused damage, access failures and the manager's existing vendor workflow
the concentration risk a single portfolio relationship creates
excluded: advising a landlord on their lease, habitability duties or tax treatment, which is outside this role
renewal negotiation and retention of a portfolio, which belongs to the renewals knowledge base

pros.claim: One relationship can place and sustain many contracts with a commercially literate decision maker who will actually read the contract
pros.example: a manager comparing the plan's after-hours dispatch against the cost of staffing their own night call handling

cons.claim: Concentration cuts both ways, because a structural mismatch discovered after placement is discovered across the whole portfolio at once
cons.example: a portfolio of older rentals producing repeated tenant-damage claims that the wear trigger was never going to answer

failure_modes: carrying owner-occupied product assumptions onto tenant-occupied properties
leaving the claim-placement and fee-payment roles undefined between owner, manager and tenant
ignoring the manager's existing vendor relationships that the obligor's network will displace
acceptance_tests: each portfolio agreement records the contract holder, who may place claims, who pays the service fee, and how tenant-caused damage and access failures are expected to be treated under the contract
revisit_triggers: the portfolio composition or occupancy mix changes
a dispute pattern appears across several properties in one portfolio
the manager changes their vendor arrangement

base.update_signal: a portfolio's composition, occupancy mix or dispute pattern changes materially, or the manager's own vendor arrangement changes

nodes.definition: Build origination relationships with the people standing in the homeowner's utility room at the moment a failure is on their mind: heating, plumbing, electrical and appliance contractors, and home inspectors who have just written up an ageing system. The structure has three pieces that are constantly confused and must be kept separate. First, origination: the trade introduces the homeowner to the plan, which raises exactly the same value-exchange questions as a transaction partner and must be papered and reviewed the same way. Second, network participation: the contractor may want to join the obligor's dispatch network, which is a relationship between the contractor and the obligor rather than a payment from the seller, and conflating the two is how informal referral money gets rationalised. Third, disclosure of interest: a contractor who recommends a plan and then receives work through that plan has an interest the homeowner is entitled to know about, and an inspector who condemns a system and sells the plan that might cover it is in a position that has to be stated out loud. Handled cleanly this is the highest-intent channel in the business; handled loosely it is the fastest route to a conflict-of-interest complaint.

included: origination relationships with trades and inspectors and the structure of any value exchange
network participation as a separate obligor-to-contractor relationship
written disclosure of the partner's interest to the homeowner
excluded: managing the obligor's contractor network or influencing its dispatch decisions
the legal review of a specific arrangement, which follows the referral-compensation class analysis

pros.claim: The trade partner is present at the highest-intent moment in the whole business and can hand over a homeowner who already understands the failure risk
pros.example: a heating technician who has just quoted a compressor repair opening the plan conversation about the rest of the systems

cons.claim: The same proximity creates a conflict of interest that, left undisclosed, damages the seller far beyond the value of the order
cons.example: an inspector who flags a failing system and sells the plan covering it without stating the connection to the homeowner

failure_modes: paying per-lead cash to a trade without the review a transaction-partner arrangement would get
letting the partner make coverage promises the seller would never make
presenting network participation as if it were compensation for referrals
acceptance_tests: each trade relationship has a papered structure, a written interest disclosure the homeowner receives, and a record that keeps origination separate from any network participation
revisit_triggers: a partner asks to change the arrangement
a homeowner complaint touches a partner's recommendation
a partner joins or leaves the obligor's network

base.update_signal: a trade partner proposes a different value exchange, or a complaint links a partner recommendation to a coverage expectation the contract did not support

nodes.definition: Treat every prospect record as carrying a provenance obligation: where it came from, what the person was told when it was captured, what they agreed to, when, and with what evidence. Sources differ sharply in the quality of that provenance - a referral from an existing client, an inbound form on the seller's own site, a co-registration or shared lead where consent was captured on someone else's page and may name a long list of unrelated partners, an aged purchased list, or a broker file with no capture record at all - and the compliance exposure runs in the same order. The working practice is to attach provenance at intake rather than reconstruct it at dial time, to keep the capture evidence for as long as the applicable rules require, to scrub against do-not-call and internal suppression lists on the cadence those rules require, and to honour an opt-out across every channel at once rather than in the system where it arrived. This is a quality decision as much as a compliance one, because leads with weak provenance convert badly and produce exactly the complaints that make the whole category harder to sell honestly.

included: a source taxonomy ordered by provenance quality
capture evidence, consent scope and retention treated as an intake-time obligation
suppression and opt-out handling applied across all channels simultaneously
excluded: asserting the current consent, retention or do-not-call requirements of any jurisdiction - verify the applicable rules and retention periods locally
the conversation that happens once contact is made, which is the direct channel node

pros.claim: Provenance attached at intake makes a later challenge answerable from the record instead of from memory
pros.example: producing the timestamped capture page and the consent language shown to a contact who says they never asked to be called

cons.claim: Insisting on provenance rules out the cheapest lead inventory and visibly shrinks the top of the funnel
cons.example: declining a low-cost aged file because the vendor cannot produce capture evidence for any record in it

failure_modes: buying leads whose consent was captured for an unrelated offer
keeping opt-outs in one channel's system only so the contact is reached again from another
discarding capture evidence before the applicable retention period ends
acceptance_tests: every lead in the system carries a source, a capture timestamp, the consent scope recorded at capture and a suppression status, and a random sample can be produced on demand
revisit_triggers: a new lead source is onboarded
a consent or opt-out dispute arises
applicable consent or retention rules change

base.update_signal: a new lead vendor is onboarded, a consent dispute is raised, or the applicable consent and retention rules change

nodes.definition: Design each channel's offer flow so that the four things buyers most often discover too late are placed structurally before the signature rather than left to the seller's goodwill in the moment: that exclusions exist and where in the document to read them, what the caps and the surrounding allowances actually are, that a service fee is payable per dispatch and generally per trade, and that the obligor decides claims under the contract. The work is concrete rather than exhortative - a one-page plain-language summary that travels with every quote, the sample contract sent before signature in every channel that allows it, a signature step preceded by an acknowledgement that the summary was received, and, in the transaction channel where the calendar compresses everything, a trigger point moved back into the listing or escrow period instead of the settlement table. The reason this is engineering rather than good intentions is that pressure peaks exactly where disclosure is hardest, and any flow that depends on the seller choosing well at the worst possible moment will fail on precisely the days it matters most.

included: the four pre-signature disclosures and their structural placement in each channel's flow
the artifacts that carry them: plain-language summary, sample contract, acknowledgement step
moving the disclosure trigger earlier in deadline-compressed channels
excluded: the clause-by-clause explanation conversation and its per-client documentation packet, which belong to the coverage-terms knowledge base
post-sale claim handling and denial conversations, which belong to the renewals and claims knowledge base

pros.claim: Structural placement makes honest disclosure the default path instead of a decision the seller has to win against a deadline
pros.example: an escrow-stage summary and sample contract arriving days before the settlement appointment rather than at it

cons.claim: Front-loading the limits costs close rate against competitors who disclose at signature, and the artifacts must be maintained per obligor and per contract version
cons.example: losing a share of price-shopping buyers who see the cap gap before they see a competitor's brochure

failure_modes: treating the obligor's fine print as the disclosure and never producing a plain-language summary
letting the transaction channel skip the summary because the calendar is tight
delivering the disclosure after signature and calling it disclosure
acceptance_tests: for every channel there is a documented pre-signature point at which the summary, the sample contract and the acknowledgement occur, and orders lacking the acknowledgement do not proceed
revisit_triggers: a contract version changes the caps, fees or claim process
a channel flow is redesigned
a complaint indicates a buyer did not understand a term before signing

base.update_signal: a contract revision, a channel flow redesign, or a complaint showing a material term was not understood before signature

nodes.definition: Recognise the buyer situations where the ordinary flow is not enough, and apply a heavier practice without waiting to be asked. The signals are situational rather than demographic: a homeowner on a fixed income for whom the contract fee competes with the very repair fund it is meant to replace, an older buyer being sold at the door or over the phone, a buyer transacting in a second language with no interpreter present, a recently bereaved homeowner handling household systems for the first time, a first-time buyer at a compressed closing table, and any buyer who cannot restate what the plan does and does not do after the summary has been given. The heavier practice is specific: slow down, put the decision in writing with an explicit cool-down before signature, invite a family member or advisor the buyer chooses, avoid same-visit closes in home-solicitation settings, never use a failure-fear framing, and be willing to decline the sale outright when the fit is not there or the buyer cannot give informed consent. Walking away from a sale belongs in this job description rather than counting as a failure of it.

included: the situational vulnerability signals to watch for in every channel
the heavier practice: cool-down, written summary, buyer-chosen third party, no same-visit close
the affirmative duty to decline a sale that cannot be understood or afforded
excluded: clinical or legal capacity assessment of any individual, which is outside the seller's competence and role
personalized financial advice about the buyer's household budget

pros.claim: A cool-down and a restatement check catch the sales that would otherwise become complaints, early cancellations and chargebacks
pros.example: a buyer who cannot restate the per-dispatch fee obligation being given the summary and a scheduled follow-up instead of a signature line

cons.claim: The practice deliberately costs volume, and the signals are judgement calls that can misfire in either direction
cons.example: delaying a fully competent older buyer who simply wanted to finish that day and found the caution patronising

failure_modes: treating age alone as the signal while missing a rushed first-time buyer at a settlement table
closing in the same visit after a door-to-door contact
continuing a sale the buyer cannot restate because the paperwork has already been started
acceptance_tests: any file carrying a vulnerability flag records the cool-down offered, the written summary delivered, and either the buyer's restatement or the decision to decline the sale
revisit_triggers: a cancellation or complaint arrives from a flagged file
a channel starts producing a different buyer mix
a new outreach method reaches buyers at home

base.update_signal: a complaint or early cancellation traced to a buyer who did not understand the purchase, or a shift in a channel's buyer mix

nodes.definition: Consolidate the obligations that are otherwise scattered across agreements, statutes and habits into one maintained matrix whose rows are channel-and-jurisdiction pairs and whose columns are obligation classes: who must be licensed, registered or appointed to work this channel here; which disclosures must be delivered and at what point in the flow; what material approval applies to this channel's templates; what contact-method and consent rules bind it; what records must be kept and for how long; which partner value-exchange structures have been reviewed; and who owns each cell. The matrix is what makes compliance auditable rather than anecdotal, and it is where verify current rules in your jurisdiction stops being a slogan and becomes a dated cell holding a verified answer, its source, the person who obtained it and the date it must be re-checked. It is built once the channels exist in outline, and it is re-reviewed on a fixed cadence and on every trigger: a new jurisdiction, a new channel, a new obligor, a new partner arrangement, or an announced regulatory change.

included: the channel-by-obligation-class matrix with owner, source and future review date per cell
the review cadence and the trigger list that forces re-review
the record-retention column that keeps evidence discoverable
excluded: asserting the content of any jurisdiction's current rules - each cell holds a locally verified answer with its date and source
substituting for legal advice; the matrix records what counsel and the obligor's compliance desk answered

pros.claim: One matrix turns a diffuse set of obligations into a checkable artifact that survives staff turnover and an audit request
pros.example: handing an obligor's compliance desk the matrix instead of a folder of recollections when they ask how outreach is controlled

cons.claim: The matrix is only as true as its last review, and a stale cell carries more false confidence than an empty one
cons.example: a jurisdiction row reviewed long ago and still relied upon after a statutory amendment

failure_modes: building the matrix and never scheduling the review
copying another seller's matrix without verifying it for your own jurisdictions and obligors
leaving cells unowned so nobody is responsible for re-verification
acceptance_tests: every live channel-and-jurisdiction pair has a populated row with a named owner, a cited source, and a review date still in the future
revisit_triggers: a new jurisdiction, channel, obligor or partner arrangement is added
a regulatory change is announced
a cell's review date arrives

base.update_signal: a regulatory change, a new channel-and-jurisdiction pair, or an expired review date on any cell

nodes.definition: Compare channels on contribution rather than on headline compensation, using a model built only from inputs the seller can actually observe in their own book. The mechanism per channel is: contracts written per period, times the compensation basis per contract taken from the current exhibit, less acquisition cost including lead spend, partner marketing under a reviewed structure, event and material cost, less the seller's own hours priced at their opportunity cost, less the servicing and dispute load the channel creates after the sale, adjusted for the channel's chargeback and early-cancellation experience and for the persistency it tends to produce. Every one of those is a measured quantity from this seller's own records rather than a borrowed benchmark, and the model exists to make the comparison honest rather than to produce a number worth quoting to anyone. Its recurring finding is that the channel with the most attractive per-contract compensation is rarely the one with the best contribution per hour once compliance load, dispute rate and cancellations are counted - and that finding is what sets the channel mix and the order in which channels get built.

included: the contribution mechanism per channel and the observable inputs it needs
chargeback, early-cancellation and dispute load as first-class inputs rather than footnotes
the resulting channel mix and build sequence
excluded: borrowing industry benchmark figures or asserting any channel's returns as a fact
renewal-book valuation and retention economics, which belong to the renewals knowledge base

pros.claim: Contribution per hour exposes the channel that looks best on the compensation schedule and worst on the calendar
pros.example: a direct channel with strong per-contract compensation falling behind a slower partner channel once acquisition hours and early cancellations are counted

cons.claim: The model needs several measurement periods of the seller's own data before it is trustworthy, and an early reading can misdirect the build sequence
cons.example: abandoning a partner channel after one weak quarter, before the relationship had produced its second wave of referrals

failure_modes: modelling with borrowed benchmarks instead of measured inputs
ignoring servicing and dispute load because it lands in a different week than the sale
treating one model output as a settled answer rather than as a decision to be re-measured
acceptance_tests: each live channel has a contribution figure built only from the seller's own measured inputs, stating the measurement period and the chargeback and cancellation inputs used
revisit_triggers: a compensation schedule changes
a channel's cancellation or dispute rate moves
a new measurement period closes

base.update_signal: a new measurement period closes, a compensation schedule changes, or a channel's chargeback and dispute rates shift

nodes.definition: Define what must be true before an order leaves the seller's desk, and package it so the next two stages of the business can work from it without re-interviewing the client. The packet carries the property and its jurisdiction; the obligor and the product version quoted; the tier and options ordered; the selected service-fee level; the effective-date rule applied and the date it produces; the payer and the payment route; the channel and the source of record; the disclosure artifacts delivered with their timestamps and the buyer's acknowledgement; any vulnerability flag and what was done about it; the reference to a reviewed partner arrangement where one applies; and the recorded compensation expectation for later reconciliation. It is a gate rather than a filing habit: an order missing the acknowledgement, the effective-date confirmation or a populated compliance-matrix row for its channel and jurisdiction does not go. It is also the handoff artifact, because the coverage-terms work and the renewal and claims-experience work both begin from what this packet says was sold and what the buyer was actually told.

included: the required contents of a complete order packet
the hard gate conditions that stop an order from being transmitted
handing a settled record to the coverage conversation and to the renewal book
excluded: the coverage conversation and per-client documentation that follow, which belong to the coverage-terms knowledge base
renewal tracking, claims-experience guidance and retention of the resulting book, which belong to the renewals knowledge base

pros.claim: A single gate catches the errors that are cheap to fix now and impossible to fix once funds have moved
pros.example: an order held because the effective-date rule was never re-confirmed after the closing date moved

cons.claim: The gate adds a step at exactly the moment every other party in a transaction wants speed, and it will occasionally cost an order
cons.example: a settlement cut-off missed because the buyer's acknowledgement was still outstanding

failure_modes: treating the packet as post-sale paperwork assembled after funding
granting a just-this-once exception at a closing
handing off a packet that does not record what the buyer was actually told
acceptance_tests: no order is transmitted without a complete packet, and a periodic sample audit shows the acknowledgement, the effective-date confirmation and the compliance-matrix row present on every transmitted order
revisit_triggers: a gate exception is granted
a downstream complaint traces back to a missing packet element
a new channel or obligor changes the required contents

base.update_signal: a gate exception is granted, a downstream complaint traces to a packet gap, or a new channel or obligor requires different packet contents

edges.why_related: you cannot say who is bound to perform until you have fixed what kind of promise the document makes
the regulatory class screen asks which statute treats this product, which presupposes a settled description of the product
what the seller must personally hold is defined by the obligation class the jurisdiction screen identifies
the boundary rule that claim outcomes belong to the obligor is only meaningful once the obligor and administrator have been identified
a line-up of systems, appliance and combined plans only parses once the category and its wear-failure trigger are fixed
caps and allowances are read per tier and option, so the mechanics sheet has to exist before the cap arithmetic can be built
the selectable fee levels and their price relationship are defined inside the obligor's line-up
you can only diligence the party you have correctly identified as the obligor, its administrator and its network owner
tier and limit selection is one of the components that assembles the quoted price
most compensation exhibits compute from the contract fee, so the price build is an input to the pay mechanism
a channel is only a candidate if the current agreement, territory and licence class permit the seller to work it
the transaction route is one mapped channel whose operating detail is built only after it is chosen as a candidate
the direct route is a mapped channel with its own buying moment and its own compliance class
the portfolio route is a mapped channel whose decision maker and servicing load were named in the map
the trade origination route is a mapped channel whose buying moment sits at the point of failure
the value-exchange question arises the moment an introducing transaction partner is recorded as the source
outbound contact in the direct channel is what creates the provenance and consent obligation on every record
the offer flow is engineered to enforce, at the artifact level, the language boundary the rule sets
the heavier practice is an escalation of the standard disclosure flow, so the standard flow must exist first
the verified compensation basis per contract is the revenue input the contribution model multiplies
the packet records the disclosure artifacts and acknowledgement that the offer design produced
the obligation class identified for a jurisdiction limits which channels can lawfully be operated there at all
edges.risk_of_conflict: a channel is scoped and staffed before anyone checks whether the product and seller are authorized in that jurisdiction

edges.why_related: the effective-date and cancellation mechanics constrain when an order may be placed and what may be said about coverage at the closing
