edges.risk_of_conflict: an order timed to the sales calendar rather than to the rule that attaches coverage to the recorded close

edges.why_related: the approved-material and territory terms of the representative agreement bound what outreach may be sent and to whom
edges.risk_of_conflict: a vendor template deployed at volume before it is inside the approved material set

edges.why_related: consent scope, suppression cadence and retention become concrete cells the matrix must carry for every outbound channel
edges.risk_of_conflict: consent practice living only in a lead system while the matrix claims the channel is controlled

edges.why_related: an order cannot be transmitted for a channel-and-jurisdiction pair that has no populated, in-date matrix row
edges.risk_of_conflict: an order written into a jurisdiction whose row was never verified or has gone stale

edges.why_related: the product with the most attractive compensation exhibit is frequently not the product with the best field performance
edges.resolution_rule: the diligence screen decides what may be carried at all; compensation may break a tie only between products that have both already passed the screen, and a product that trips a written stop condition is dropped regardless of what it pays

edges.why_related: the escrow calendar compresses exactly the window in which caps, fees and exclusions need to be surfaced before signature
edges.resolution_rule: disclosure wins: the trigger point moves back into the listing or escrow period, and if the summary and acknowledgement cannot be completed before signature the order waits for the next available signing rather than being written unacknowledged

edges.why_related: partners expect the informal per-deal value that competitors offer, while only reviewed structures survive scrutiny
edges.resolution_rule: compliance wins: only arrangements reviewed by counsel and the obligor's compliance desk are entered, and a partner who will work only on an unreviewable arrangement is declined even at the cost of the channel volume

edges.why_related: an origination partner standing next to a broken system will happily promise coverage the seller would never promise
edges.resolution_rule: the boundary governs the whole channel: partners hand over only seller-supplied materials, the interest disclosure travels with every referral, and a partner who keeps making coverage promises is removed from origination

edges.why_related: a high per-dispatch fee buys a lower headline contract price while raising the buyer's real cost of using the plan
edges.resolution_rule: quote the first-year total with both components shown separately and let the buyer choose the fee level on their own expected usage; never select the fee option that maximises the compensation base

edges.why_related: same-visit and same-call conversion is what makes direct outreach economic, and it is precisely what the safeguards remove
edges.resolution_rule: the safeguards win wherever a signal is present: no same-visit close in a home-solicitation setting, a written summary and cool-down before signature, and the sale declined outright if the buyer cannot restate what the plan does

edges.why_related: an obligor's field performance drives the dispute and servicing load that determines a channel's real contribution
edges.example: slow authorisations on a carried product turning a high-volume partner channel into an unpaid support desk

edges.why_related: the per-dispatch fee is one of the most commonly under-disclosed costs, which is why it becomes a named element of the pre-signature summary
edges.example: buyers who learn only at the first dispatch that a second trade means a second fee

edges.why_related: the buying moment and cycle length recorded in the map determine the acquisition hours and lead spend the model has to absorb
edges.example: a trigger-based direct channel needing many more contacts per contract than a channel with a built-in transaction event

edges.why_related: a partner arrangement must be reviewed and papered before its row and evidence pointers can be entered in the matrix
the effective-date rule is applied and confirmed against the document before the packet can be completed and transmitted
packet audits show where the flow lets disclosure slip, which sends the offer design back for repair rather than blaming the individual sale
edges.benefit_of_coupling: recurring gaps become flow changes instead of reminders

edges.why_related: both are intermediated channels where a commercial party stands between the seller and the occupant, so both share partner-management, interest-disclosure and concentration practice

conflict_axes.name: compensation_pull_versus_product_fit
conflict_axes.description: The product with the richest compensation exhibit is frequently not the one whose obligor performs best in the counties the seller works, and the pull is felt on every single quote rather than once at onboarding.
poles: lead with the product that pays best
lead with the product that performs best for this property
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: let the diligence screen decide the carried menu and let compensation break ties only inside it; audit which product the seller has been leading with each quarter

conflict_axes.name: closing_speed_versus_pre_signature_disclosure
conflict_axes.description: The transaction channel's value comes from the deadline and the closing funds, and the deadline is exactly what squeezes out the cap, fee and exclusion conversation.
poles: capture the order before the settlement cut-off
complete the disclosure before any signature
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: move the disclosure trigger back into listing or escrow so both can be satisfied, and let an order wait rather than be written unacknowledged

conflict_axes.name: headline_price_versus_total_first_year_cost
conflict_axes.description: A higher per-dispatch service fee lowers the contract fee that gets compared against competitors, while raising what the buyer actually pays to use the plan.
poles: quote the lowest comparable contract fee
quote the honest first-year total including dispatch fees
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: always show both components and the crossover, and let the buyer choose the fee level on their own expected usage rather than on the comparison optics

conflict_axes.name: channel_volume_versus_compliance_load
conflict_axes.description: The channels that produce the most orders per hour are usually the ones carrying the heaviest licensing, consent, disclosure and recordkeeping obligations.
poles: open the channel that produces volume now
open only the channels whose obligations are already met
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat compliance load as a modelled cost of the channel rather than as a hurdle to be argued down, and close a channel whose obligations cannot be met rather than running it thin

conflict_axes.name: partner_relationship_versus_referral_compliance
conflict_axes.description: Origination partners in both the transaction and trade channels expect the informal per-deal value that looser competitors provide, while only papered and reviewed structures survive being examined.
poles: keep the partner who drives volume
keep only arrangements that survive review
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: offer reviewable structures early and decline the relationship rather than the review; document what was offered and refused

conflict_axes.name: whose_client_is_it_in_a_transaction
conflict_axes.description: In the closing channel the introducing agent supplies the volume and the homeowner bears the consequences, and their interests diverge exactly at the disclosure moment.
poles: serve the introducing transaction partner who sends the work
serve the homeowner who will live with the contract
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the homeowner's informed consent governs the sale while the partner relationship is served by reliability and speed everywhere else in the process

conflict_axes.name: single_obligor_depth_versus_multi_obligor_choice
conflict_axes.description: Carrying one obligor buys schedule depth, product fluency and often better terms, while carrying several buys the ability to place a property with whoever actually performs in that county.
poles: concentrate on one obligor
carry several obligors
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: let network depth by county and the written stop conditions decide, and accept the administrative cost of a second obligor where the first cannot serve a market

conflict_axes.name: lead_volume_versus_consent_quality
conflict_axes.description: The cheapest and largest lead inventory is precisely the inventory whose capture evidence and consent scope cannot be produced when challenged.
poles: buy the volume the funnel needs
buy only records whose provenance can be produced
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: make capture evidence a purchase condition and price the risk of unprovenanced records as a channel cost rather than a compliance abstraction

conflict_axes.name: urgency_that_informs_versus_fear_that_sells
conflict_axes.description: There are legitimate timing facts in this business, such as a rate schedule changing or a transaction window closing, and there is manufactured dread about a specific system failing next winter, and the two are easy to blur under quota pressure.
poles: create urgency to close now
state only timing facts that are true and verifiable
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: permit only urgency a buyer could verify independently, ban failure-fear framings by name in every script, and audit templates rather than trusting intent

conflict_axes.name: portfolio_concentration_versus_relationship_dependence
conflict_axes.description: A property manager or a single high-volume trade partner can supply a large share of the book, which is efficient until that one relationship or its opinion of the obligor turns.
poles: grow the relationship that produces most of the volume
keep the book diversified across channels and partners
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: model concentration explicitly as a channel risk input and keep at least one independent origination path alive even when the dominant relationship is healthy

edge_cases.description: A referral arrives for a property in a jurisdiction where the obligor has no filing or the seller has no authorization, and the transaction is already in escrow
edge_cases.trigger: an out-of-area property enters the pipeline before the jurisdiction screen for it is complete
edge_cases.mitigation: decline or hand the order to a seller authorized there, tell the partner why in writing, and never assume authority travels with the seller across a state line

edge_cases.description: The closing date moves and the effective-date rule leaves a window in which the buyer believes they are covered and the contract says otherwise
edge_cases.trigger: a rescheduled or delayed recording after the order was placed
edge_cases.mitigation: re-confirm the effective-date rule against the document on every date change, restate it in writing to the buyer, and hold the packet until the confirmation is recorded

edge_cases.description: A newly built home already carries builder and manufacturer coverage on most of the systems the plan would duplicate
edge_cases.trigger: a new-construction or recently-replaced-systems property enters the channel
edge_cases.mitigation: map the coverage the buyer already holds before quoting, say plainly where the plan would overlap, and either reduce the offer to the genuinely uncovered exposure or advise waiting

edge_cases.description: A transaction partner asks for a plan to be placed on a home with a system that has already failed, so the buyer will be covered
edge_cases.trigger: a known existing failure disclosed during the transaction
edge_cases.mitigation: state that the contract responds to failure from normal wear under its own conditions, refuse to represent that a known existing failure will be paid, put the question to the obligor in writing if the buyer still wants the plan, and record what was said to whom

edge_cases.description: A buyer at the signing asks whether everything in the house is now covered
edge_cases.trigger: the reassurance question at the moment of signature
edge_cases.mitigation: answer from the document by opening the covered-items list, the exclusions heading and the cap table, and record that the summary was shown rather than paraphrasing a yes

edge_cases.description: A property manager expects tenant-caused damage and after-hours tenant calls to be absorbed by the plan
edge_cases.trigger: a portfolio placement where the occupant is not the contract holder
edge_cases.mitigation: write the claim-placement, access and fee-payment roles into the agreement, state before placement how the wear trigger treats tenant-caused damage, and decline the portfolio if the expectation cannot be corrected

edge_cases.description: A trade partner asks for cash per referral, framed as a thank-you or as a fee for the introduction
edge_cases.trigger: an origination partner proposes an informal value exchange
edge_cases.mitigation: pause the arrangement, run the class analysis and obtain a review, offer a reviewable structure instead, and record the refusal if the partner declines it

edge_cases.description: A purchased lead file turns out to have no capture evidence and produces contacts who say they never consented
edge_cases.trigger: an aged or brokered list is loaded into the dialer
edge_cases.mitigation: suspend the source immediately, quarantine the records, honour every opt-out across all systems at once, and require capture evidence as a purchase condition before any future file

edge_cases.description: An obligor revises its cap table or fee levels while quotes from the previous schedule are still outstanding with buyers
edge_cases.trigger: a mid-cycle product or rate revision
edge_cases.mitigation: re-quote from the current schedule rather than adjusting the old one, reissue the plain-language summary for the new version, and tell affected buyers what changed before any signature

edge_cases.description: A carried obligor shows signs of distress or changes administrator, and the in-force book is affected while the seller has no authority over any of it
edge_cases.trigger: a regulator action, ownership change or a sudden cluster of dispatch failures
edge_cases.mitigation: stop writing new business on that product against the written stop conditions, re-map the party and backing structure, tell clients factually what changed without predicting outcomes, and route the escalation path the agreement provides

edge_cases.description: A marketing vendor offers a mailer template designed to read like an expiring-warranty notice
edge_cases.trigger: an outreach template arrives from a vendor or an upline rather than from the obligor's approved set
edge_cases.mitigation: reject the template outright as a banned framing, use only materials inside the approved set, and record the rejection so the same template does not return through another channel

edge_cases.description: An older homeowner contacted at the door wants to sign the same evening and waves away the summary
edge_cases.trigger: a home-solicitation contact meeting one or more vulnerability signals
edge_cases.mitigation: leave the written summary, decline the same-visit signature, offer a scheduled follow-up and a buyer-chosen third party, and record the flag and the outcome in the packet

workflow.action: Fix the product category and the naming discipline
workflow.description: State what the contract promises, what triggers the obligor's duty, and which adjacent products it is not
workflow.artifact: product category statement with the banned-vocabulary list
workflow.gate: the seller can state the performance trigger in one sentence and name two products this is not without using insurance as a synonym

workflow.action: Map the parties behind every carried product
workflow.description: Identify obligor, administrator, backing arrangement, network owner and the seller's own role from the contract text
workflow.artifact: party and liability map per product
workflow.gate: each party is cited to a clause or filing and the seller's non-obligation to perform is written down

workflow.action: Screen the regulatory class for every jurisdiction in the pipeline
workflow.description: Identify the obligation classes and put the open questions to the regulator, the obligor and counsel
workflow.artifact: dated jurisdiction obligation screen with sources and open questions
workflow.gate: every pipeline jurisdiction has a dated record naming its obligation classes, its sources and its unresolved questions

workflow.description: Collect appointments, territory grants, approved-material versions, licence status and renewal dates
workflow.artifact: authorization file with a renewal calendar
workflow.gate: every obligor-and-jurisdiction pair shows a current agreement, the material versions in use, and a future review date

workflow.action: Diligence and shortlist the obligors worth carrying
workflow.description: Assess backing, registration standing, county-level network depth, administrator responsiveness and complaint pattern
workflow.artifact: carried-products shortlist with written reasons and stop conditions
workflow.gate: each shortlisted product has a dated diligence note and explicit stop conditions

workflow.action: Build the product mechanics sheet for each carried line-up
workflow.description: Record what each tier and option adds, which limit moves and what condition attaches
workflow.gate: every currently sellable tier and option appears on the sheet and the sheet date is inside the obligor's revision cycle

workflow.action: Build the exposure worksheet from caps, allowances and fee levels
workflow.description: Turn the cap table and allowance structure into worst-case gap arithmetic for a major system
workflow.gate: the arithmetic uses only the contract's own cap table and a locally verified replacement cost range, with no figure recited from memory

workflow.action: Verify the compensation mechanism per product and channel
workflow.description: Read the compensation exhibit, record how each component is triggered, and set up the per-deal reconciliation
workflow.artifact: compensation mechanism worksheet with a reconciliation log
workflow.gate: every carried product and channel has its basis and chargeback conditions recorded from the exhibit rather than from an illustration

workflow.action: Map the channels and screen each for buildability
workflow.description: Name buying moment, decision maker, cycle length, compliance class and servicing load per route
workflow.gate: each route is marked buildable or not buildable against the dated authorization file with a reason

workflow.description: Populate every live channel-and-jurisdiction row with its obligation classes, owner, source and review date
workflow.gate: no live channel-and-jurisdiction pair has an empty, unowned or out-of-date row

workflow.action: Engineer the disclosure-first offer flow into every channel
workflow.description: Place the summary, sample contract and acknowledgement before signature, moving the trigger earlier where the calendar compresses
workflow.artifact: per-channel offer flow with named disclosure artifacts and trigger points
workflow.gate: each channel has a documented pre-signature point and the order path physically blocks an unacknowledged signature

workflow.action: Gate the order packet before anything is transmitted
workflow.description: Assemble the packet and check the hard gate conditions before the order leaves the desk
workflow.artifact: complete order packet ready for handoff
workflow.gate: the packet shows the acknowledgement, the confirmed effective date, the compliance-matrix row, any vulnerability flag and the recorded compensation expectation

dominance_rules.rule: Jurisdiction authorization dominates every channel and revenue consideration
dominance_rules.rationale: an unauthorized sale is not a discounted sale, it is an unwindable one that can cost the appointment and the licence
dominance_rules.trigger: a property, partner or lead sits in a jurisdiction whose screen is incomplete or whose obligation classes are unmet
dominance_rules.action: stop, complete the screen, and decline or refer the business rather than writing it on an assumption

dominance_rules.rationale: the buyer's informed consent is the only thing that makes the sale defensible afterwards, and the deadline belongs to the transaction rather than to the buyer
dominance_rules.trigger: a settlement or partner deadline cannot be met with the summary and acknowledgement completed
dominance_rules.action: move the disclosure trigger earlier, and if that is impossible let the order wait or go unwritten

dominance_rules.rule: The written contract dominates every verbal representation
dominance_rules.rationale: the obligor performs to the document, so anything said beyond it is a promise the seller cannot keep and the buyer cannot enforce
dominance_rules.trigger: a buyer question invites a reassurance the contract does not support
dominance_rules.action: open the clause, show it, and record that it was shown rather than paraphrasing it into a yes

dominance_rules.rule: Claim outcomes belong to the obligor and dominate any seller prediction
dominance_rules.rationale: the seller has no adjudication authority and a predicted outcome becomes the buyer's expectation and the seller's liability
dominance_rules.trigger: anyone asks the seller whether a specific failure will be covered or replaced
dominance_rules.action: explain the process and the contract language, name the obligor as the decision maker, and decline to predict the outcome

dominance_rules.rule: Obligor field performance dominates compensation attractiveness in deciding what to carry
dominance_rules.rationale: the seller inherits the reputational consequence of dispatch and authorisation failures while holding none of the obligor's authority
dominance_rules.trigger: a product with a better compensation exhibit fails or approaches a written stop condition on the diligence screen
dominance_rules.action: keep it off the carried menu, or remove it, whatever the schedule pays

dominance_rules.rule: Reviewed value-exchange structures dominate partner relationship pressure
dominance_rules.rationale: an unreviewed referral arrangement puts the appointment, the licence and the partner in jeopardy at once and cannot be undone quietly
dominance_rules.trigger: a transaction or trade partner proposes or expects an arrangement outside the reviewed set
dominance_rules.action: offer a reviewable structure, and decline the relationship rather than the review

dominance_rules.rule: Consent and suppression records dominate lead volume targets
dominance_rules.rationale: records with no provenance are the ones that generate complaints, and the funnel gain never covers the exposure
dominance_rules.trigger: a lead source cannot produce capture evidence or a suppression request is pending
dominance_rules.action: suspend the source and quarantine the records before any further contact

dominance_rules.rule: Vulnerable-buyer safeguards dominate same-visit and same-call conversion
dominance_rules.rationale: a sale a buyer cannot restate is a cancellation, a complaint and a chargeback that has not happened yet
dominance_rules.trigger: any situational vulnerability signal appears in a home-solicitation, telephone or compressed closing setting
dominance_rules.action: leave the written summary, apply the cool-down, invite a buyer-chosen third party, and decline the sale if informed consent is not there

dominance_rules.rule: Avoiding duplicate coverage dominates the available order
dominance_rules.rationale: selling a buyer protection they already hold is the clearest form of the category's core ethical failure and it is discovered at the first claim
dominance_rules.trigger: the property is new construction, has recently replaced systems, or the buyer holds live manufacturer or builder coverage
dominance_rules.action: map the existing coverage first and reduce, defer or decline the offer to the genuinely uncovered exposure

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run the jurisdiction class screen and confirm your own authorization before building any pipeline in a new area
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a partner network, lead spend and a set of written orders that all have to be unwound because the product or the seller was never authorized there

anti_rework_rules.rule: Read the cap table, allowance structure and fee levels before quoting anything to anyone
anti_rework_rules.prevents: quotes and expectations built on remembered numbers that have to be corrected after the buyer has already decided

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm the effective-date rule from the document before promising coverage tied to a closing date
anti_rework_rules.prevents: the coverage gap that surfaces only when a claim lands in it and can no longer be repaired

anti_rework_rules.rule: Get any partner value-exchange structure reviewed before the first order flows through it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: unwinding an arrangement and repaying value with the partner, the obligor and possibly a regulator all watching

anti_rework_rules.rule: Attach source, consent scope and capture evidence at lead intake rather than at dial time
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a whole file of contacts that has to be quarantined because nobody can show what was agreed at capture

anti_rework_rules.rule: Diligence the obligor's county-level network depth before entering a market with it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a book of clients in an area where authorised work cannot actually be dispatched, which no sales effort can repair

anti_rework_rules.rule: Build the channel compliance matrix before scaling any channel past a handful of orders
anti_rework_rules.prevents: retrofitting disclosures, consent records and material approvals across business already written

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify the compensation basis and channel codes per product before modelling channel economics
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a channel mix decision and a build sequence founded on a compensation assumption the exhibit never supported

anti_rework_rules.rule: Put the disclosure artifacts into each channel flow before running volume through it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a cohort of contracts sold without acknowledgement that then produces the complaints and cancellations the flow existed to avoid

iteration_protocol.trigger: an obligor revises its product line-up, cap table, fee levels or rate schedule
iteration_protocol.action: refresh the mechanics sheet and exposure worksheet, re-quote anything outstanding from the current schedule, and reissue the plain-language summary for the new version

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new jurisdiction is entered or a regulatory change is announced for one already in the book
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the class screen, re-check the authorization file, and update every affected row of the compliance matrix with its new source and review date

iteration_protocol.trigger: client-reported dispatch or authorisation failures cluster on a carried product
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the diligence screen against the written stop conditions, re-map the party structure if the administrator changed, and decide whether to stop writing new business on it

iteration_protocol.trigger: a complaint or early cancellation indicates a buyer did not understand a material term before signing
iteration_protocol.action: audit that channel's offer flow rather than the individual sale, move the disclosure trigger earlier, and re-check every script and template against the boundary

iteration_protocol.trigger: a lead source produces consent disputes, opt-out failures or an unusual complaint rate
iteration_protocol.action: suspend the source, quarantine and re-audit its records, and re-check the suppression cadence across every channel at once

iteration_protocol.trigger: a partner proposes an arrangement outside the reviewed set, or an existing arrangement changes
iteration_protocol.action: pause the arrangement, re-run the class analysis, obtain a fresh review, and update the matrix row and the payment record before any further orders

iteration_protocol.trigger: a measurement period closes or a channel's chargeback and dispute rates move materially
iteration_protocol.action: re-measure contribution per hour from the seller's own records, and re-sequence, throttle or close channels on the new reading rather than on the headline schedule

priority_rationale: The frame nodes come first because nothing downstream is decidable until the product category, the party who is actually bound to perform, the jurisdiction's obligation class, the seller's own authorization and the outer boundary of what may be said are all settled; product mechanics (tiers, caps, fees, term and cancellation) and obligor diligence follow because they define what is being sold and by whom; price and compensation mechanics sit above those because both are computed from the product's own components; the channel nodes come next because a channel is only buildable once authorization, product and compliance class are known, and each channel drags its own obligations and disclosure difficulty behind it; and disclosure design, vulnerable-buyer safeguards, the compliance matrix, the contribution model and the order-packet gate come last because they compose everything above into an offer that can be made honestly, audited, measured and handed off to the coverage conversation and the renewal book.
